content.title: March Madness 2026: Teams, players, schedule and how to watch the men’s NCAA tournament
content.text: The 68-team NCAA men’s tournament begins this week, launching another edition of March Madness. From title favourites to potential Cinderella runs, here are the teams, players and storylines to watch.Picture by Sam Hodde/Getty ImagesBy Will Imbo 16 March 2026 12:55 GMT+05 min readMarch Madness returns this week as the 2026 NCAA men’s basketball tournament gets underway, with 68 teams battling through a single-elimination bracket for a place in the Final Four and a shot at the national title. This year’s field features several dominant contenders, including Duke, Michigan, Arizona and defending champion Florida, who earned the No. 1 seeds after standout seasons. But as always in March Madness, the tournament’s unpredictability means the spotlight can quickly shift once the first upset lands and an unheralded player emerges as a tournament star. Here’s a look at the teams, players and key storylines to follow as the road to the 2026 NCAA championship begins. What is March Madness? Explaining the NCAA men's basketball tournament Picture by Jamie Squire/Getty ImagesSAN ANTONIO, TEXAS - APRIL 07: The Florida Gators celebrate after defeating the Houston Cougars in the 2025 National Championship.Top teams and contenders to watch The 2026 bracket is headlined by four dominant programs and the No. 1 seeds for the tournament: Duke, Michigan, Arizona, and defending champions Florida. Duke enters March Madness as the top overall seed after a dominant 32–2 season and an ACC tournament title. The Blue Devils have been one of the most consistent teams in the country and will look to translate that form into a deep tournament run after reaching the Sweet 16 (the final 16 teams in the tournament) in each of the past two tournaments. Duke is also a five-time national champion, most recently winning the title in 2015. Arizona claimed the No. 1 seed in the West region after matching Duke’s 32–2 record. The Wildcats opened the season with 23 straight wins and built one of the deepest rosters in the field, with key victories over fellow contenders including Florida, UConn, Alabama, Houston and Kansas. Arizona is chasing its first national title since 1997, with the program still seeking its first Final Four appearance since 2001. Michigan secured the Midwest region’s No. 1 seed after a 31–3 season, despite falling to Purdue in the Big Ten tournament title game. The Wolverines lost only twice in the regular season and built their résumé around a physically imposing lineup, defensive efficiency and consistent play across the season. Michigan is now aiming for its first Final Four since 2018 and its first national title since 1989. Florida, the defending national champion, returns as the No. 1 seed in the South region after going 26–7 and winning the SEC regular-season title. The Gators found their rhythm late, closing the regular season on an 11-game winning streak, and now have a chance to become the first men’s team since UConn in 2024 to successfully defend the NCAA title. Florida won back-to-back championships in 2006 and 2007, then lifted the trophy again last year.Picture by Jacob Kupferman/Getty ImagesThe Duke Blue Devils celebrate after winning the 2026 ACC Tournament.Beyond the top seeds, several challengers could also make a serious run. Houston enters at 28–6 after reaching last season’s national title game and carries the longest active Sweet 16 streak in the country at six straight appearances. Purdue, now 27–8, heads into the tournament off a Big Ten tournament title and with one of the nation’s best offenses, while Illinois arrives at 24–8 with the country’s most productive attack and the profile of a dangerous No. 3 seed.Key players who could shape the tournament March Madness often turns college basketball’s biggest talents into household names, and the 2026 tournament features several players capable of shaping the title race. Cameron Boozer (Duke) arrives as one of the standout players in the field. The freshman forward averaged 22.7 points and 10.2 rebounds per game during the regular season while shooting 41 per cent from three-point range, helping power Duke’s run to the top overall seed. Boozer is the son of former NBA forward Carlos Boozer, a two-time All-Star and Beijing 2008 Olympic gold medallist, and is widely projected as a top lottery pick in this year’s NBA Draft.Picture by Jared C. Tilton/Getty ImagesCameron Boozer #12 of the Duke Blue Devils.Elsewhere, AJ Dybantsa (BYU) is one of the most highly touted prospects in college basketball. The Big 12 Rookie of the Year led the nation in scoring as a freshman and produced a string of standout performances late in the season, including 43 points against Utah and 40 in the Big 12 tournament against Kansas State. Like Boozer, the 6-foot-9 (2.10 metre) wing is widely projected to be among the top picks in the 2026 NBA Draft. Another player firmly in the draft conversation is Darryn Peterson (Kansas). The freshman guard averaged 19.9 points and 4.2 rebounds and entered the season as one of the leading candidates to be selected first overall in the NBA Draft. Injuries disrupted parts of his campaign, but Peterson remains one of the most gifted offensive players in the class and could further boost his draft stock with a strong tournament run.Picture by Ed Zurga/Getty ImagesDarryn Peterson #22 of the Kansas Jayhawks and forward AJ Dybantsa #3 of the BYU Cougars.When does March Madness 2026 take place? The 2026 NCAA men’s basketball tournament begins with the First Four games on 17–18 March, before the full 64-team bracket gets underway later that week. The first and second rounds run from 19–22 March, with teams competing for places in the Sweet 16, the stage featuring the final 16 teams in the tournament. The competition then moves to the regional semi-finals and finals before the Final Four in Indianapolis, where the remaining teams battle for a place in the national championship game. The 2026 title game is scheduled for 6 April.How to watch the 2026 NCAA men’s basketball tournament The 2026 NCAA men’s basketball tournament will be broadcast across multiple television networks in the United States, including CBS, TBS, TNT and truTV. Games will also be available to stream through the NCAA March Madness Live app and participating broadcast platforms. International viewing options vary by territory, with many games available through regional sports broadcasters or streaming services carrying NCAA basketball coverage. Fans can also follow live scores, highlights and bracket updates throughout the tournament via the NCAA’s official digital platforms.
